verses.text: “Listen to me, you who follow after righteousness, you who seek Yahweh: look to the rock you were cut from, and to the quarry you were dug from.
Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who bore you; for when he was but one I called him, and I blessed him, and made him many.

For Yahweh has comforted Zion. He has comforted all her waste places, and has made her wilderness like Eden, and her desert like the garden of Yahweh. Joy and gladness will be found therein, thanksgiving, and the voice of melody.
“Listen to me, my people; and hear me, my nation: for a law will go out from me, and I will establish my justice for a light to the peoples.
My righteousness is near. My salvation has gone out, and my arms will judge the peoples. The islands will wait for me, and they will trust my arm.

Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look on the earth beneath; for the heavens will vanish away like smoke, and the earth will wear out like a garment; and its inhabitants will die in the same way: but my salvation will be forever, and my righteousness will not be abolished.
“Listen to me, you who know righteousness, the people in whose heart is my law: Don’t fear the reproach of men, and don’t be dismayed at their insults.
For the moth will eat them up like a garment, and the worm will eat them like wool; but my righteousness will be forever, and my salvation to all generations.”
Awake, awake, put on strength, arm of Yahweh! Awake, as in the days of old, the generations of ancient times. Isn’t it you who cut Rahab in pieces, who pierced the monster?
Isn’t it you who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep; who made the depths of the sea a way for the redeemed to pass over?
Those ransomed by Yahweh will return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting joy shall be on their heads. They will obtain gladness and joy. Sorrow and sighing shall flee away.
“I, even I, am he who comforts you. Who are you, that you are afraid of man who shall die, and of the son of man who will be made as grass?

Have you forgotten Yahweh your Maker, who stretched out the heavens, and laid the foundations of the earth? Do you live in fear continually all day because of the fury of the oppressor, when he prepares to destroy? Where is the fury of the oppressor?
The captive exile will speedily be freed; and he will not die and go down into the pit, and his bread will not fail.
For I am Yahweh your God, who stirs up the sea, so that its waves roar: Yahweh of Armies is his name.
I have put my words in your mouth, and have covered you in the shadow of my hand, that I may plant the heavens, and lay the foundations of the earth, and tell Zion, ‘You are my people.’”
Awake, awake! Stand up, Jerusalem, you who have drunk from Yahweh’s hand the cup of his wrath. You have drunken the bowl of the cup of staggering, and drained it.
There is no one to guide her among all the sons to whom she has given birth; and there is no one who takes her by the hand among all the sons who she has brought up.
These two things have happened to you — who will grieve with you? — desolation and destruction, and famine and the sword. How can I comfort you?
Your sons have fainted. They lie at the head of all the streets, like an antelope in a net. They are full of the Yahweh’s wrath, the rebuke of your God.
Therefore now hear this, you afflicted, and drunken, but not with wine:

Thus says your Lord Yahweh, your God who pleads the cause of his people, “Behold, I have taken out of your hand the cup of staggering, even the bowl of the cup of my wrath. You will not drink it any more:

and I will put it into the hand of those who afflict you, who have said to your soul, ‘Bow down, that we may walk over you;’ and you have laid your back as the ground, like a street to those who walk over.”

footnotes.content: Look back at what made you, the prophet says—the rock you were hewn from. We are shaped by God's grace in the past, not just our present circumstance. When you forget your foundation, fear and drift follow.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham—one man, called and blessed—became many. That same God who multiplied him still keeps His word. The promises given in the desert haven't expired, even now in exile.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Desolation will become Eden; wastelands bloom again. This isn't just poetry—it's God's habit. He comforts those stripped bare. Listen for the song returning where silence dwells.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God's justice will light the nations. Not hidden, not distant—a beacon. My people, hear me: what looks like ending is seed-time for something seen afar.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: My salvation is already on the move. His arm judges—not to destroy, but to defend those who wait upon Him. Even the islands, far as they seem, sense His nearness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The heavens will smoke away, earth worn thin as cloth. But His salvation lasts. When everything familiar crumbles, cling to the one thing that outlasts all. That's not faith in doctrine—that's faith in Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't fear reproach. Men's insults are small stones; they pass. But you—you carry God's law in your heart. Let that steady you when scorn comes close.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The moth and worm finish what men begin—all passes into dust. But His righteousness is forever. One feeds the moment; one feeds all generations. Choose what lasts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Awake!" the prophet cries to God's arm. He cut Rahab—Egypt's monster, bondage itself—in pieces. That same power sleeps not. He did it once; He does it still.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Red Sea dried before Him. He made a pathway through the impossible. Every sea crossed since bears His fingerprint. Trust the God who rehearsed deliverance long ago.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The ransomed return with singing. Sorrow flees. Joy becomes their crown. This isn't comfort of words; it's the joy of homecoming. That's what waits for those who hold on.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I am He who comforts you. Why fear men who wither like grass? The voice that speaks is the one who made grass, time, and death itself. Compare what small thing you fear to what great Thing holds you.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Have you forgotten? He stretched the heavens. He laid earth's foundations. And you live in dread of one man's fury? Measure the threat against your Maker. Fear is a lie when we remember who made all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The captive will be freed soon. Death and the pit won't claim him. Bread won't fail. This is promise, plain as bread in hand. Hold it when the way looks dark.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh stirs the sea; waves obey Him. He is not merely mighty—He is Yahweh of Armies, the One who commands all power. In His name lies your shelter.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He puts His words in your mouth. He covers you in shadow—protection and nearness in one gesture. And through you, He plants heavens and founds earth. You are His vessel. Don't forget that when you feel small.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jerusalem has drunk God's wrath—the bitter cup, drained to the last drop. The weight of judgment is real, the suffering true. But see: she drank it from His hand. Even punishment speaks His care.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No one guides her children, no one holds her hand. Complete abandonment—mothers and fathers gone, alone in the wreckage. This is exile's real face: not policy but grief.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Desolation, destruction, famine, sword—a cascade of loss. Who will grieve with her? But even as Isaiah speaks this, he asks: How can I comfort you? The question itself turns us toward the One who can.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons faint in the streets, trapped like antelope. They are full of His wrath, bearing His rebuke. Judgment falls on a whole people. And yet—His eyes are on them still. Even in wrath, not forgotten.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Afflicted and drunken—drunk with sorrow, staggering under weight. Not drunken with wine, but with God's judgment. Yet the word begins: "Hear this." Even in this state, hope has a voice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The cup is taken from your hand. God Himself pleads your cause and removes the judgment. Looking back, readers today hear an echo of One who bore the cup we could not—Jesus, in Gethsemane, who drank what we could not drink. His hand takes it from ours.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The oppressors' cup will come to them. Their own cruelty will be their drink. You who lay down your back as ground will rise again. Justice turns. This is not revenge fantasy—it's the sober promise of a God who sees all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
